name: Tejas Networks Ltd
title: Tejas Networks Ltd - 540595 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: FY26 was a loss-making transition year: revenue ₹1,103 cr and PAT loss ₹909 cr, with inventory ₹2,438 cr and receivables ₹3,258 cr; no numeric guidance, only a 'goal' of PAT-positive FY27.

summary.headline: Tejas Networks Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8% QoQ to INR333 crores, but Q4 PAT loss widened to INR211 crores; FY26 PAT loss INR909 crores.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR333 crores, up 8% QoQ from INR307 crores, with EBIT loss narrowing to INR219 crores from INR239 crores. PAT loss widened to INR211 crores from INR197 crores in Q3, and FY26 revenue was INR1,103 crores against a PAT loss of INR909 crores. Management described FY26 as a transition year after the BSNL 4G project, with delayed wireline and wireless projects causing a revenue shortfall, while R&D and capex were maintained. Order book closed at INR1,514 crores versus INR1,019 crores a year earlier, with India at about 88% of revenue and around 83% of order book, excluding the BSNL 4G add-on PO. Senior management and CFO changes were announced during the call.

financial_highlights.value: INR69 crores, total INR469 crores for FY25

segments.name: Wireline
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue was driven largely by wireline sales to Indian private and international customers. Shipped significant IP/MPLS routers for BharatNet Phase III, where Tejas is the largest supplier by number of circles; supplied 100G and 400G WDM systems to a Tier-1 telco.

segments.name: Wireless
segments.commentary: Signed agreement with NEC to manufacture and supply 5G Massive MIMO radios for a global customer; first PO is in the INR1,514 crores order book and revenue is expected in FY27. Received initial 4G expansion order from a South Asian customer, with some revenue booked in FY26. Multiple 4G/5G RAN field trials ongoing in South Asia and Americas; 5G POC completed in South America.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or profit guidance given; management said it has never provided numerical guidance.
Stated goal of breakeven/PAT-positive in FY27 and PAT-positive by FY28 when asked; management said it expects better financial results in FY27 with current investments and cost structure.
Expects a good portion of the INR1,514 crore order book to convert to revenue in FY27.
Expects 5G Massive MIMO revenue from NEC contract to flow in FY27 and further 4G expansion from South Asian customer in FY27.
Expects remaining BSNL 4G collections to significantly happen in FY27, with receivables to progressively decline over the next few quarters.
R&D investment to continue but be tailored to business outlook; cost optimisation to be monitored through FY27.
Intangibles under development (up from INR400 crores to INR960 crores) expected to reach milestones over the next one to two quarters, with capitalisation on commercialisation.
capex_capacity: Intangibles under development rose from INR400 crores to INR960 crores; includes product development and technology licence/transfer from NEC; large part done, balance linked to milestones expected within one to two quarters.

Inventory of INR2,438 crores, largely procured in advance for the BSNL 4G add-on order (about 18,000 sites); inventory is usable across other 4G/4G-upgradeable-to-5G radio opportunities including private 4G networks abroad.

Product roadmap includes 1.2 Tbps per channel optical scaling to 1.6 Tbps; 5G 64TR Massive MIMO radio launched at India Mobile Congress; C+L band WDM system transmitting 76 Tbps over a single fibre pair; cloud-native converged 4G/5G core in multi-location trials; hyperscalable data center interconnect platform with over 50 Tbps in a compact footprint.
BSNL 4G/5G network went live across 100,000 sites in 2025.
Headcount approximately 2,300, broadly unchanged year on year.
demand_pricing: Order book INR1,514 crores at end Q4 FY26, about 83% India-based per analyst; excludes BSNL 4G add-on PO (about 18,000 sites), which remains under discussion with BSNL.

Management did not share deal-specific values for the NEC Massive MIMO or South Asia 4G orders; said international wireless opportunities are substantial but smaller per deal than BSNL's 100,000-site project.

Memory prices have risen; management said memory is a small share of BOM (BOM is several thousand dollars per product), and Tejas is renegotiating prices with customers and using long-term supplier contracts to protect margins.
Management said AI traffic and edge inferencing are expected to drive a network build-out cycle, with demand for 400G/800G optical and multi-terabit data centre interconnect.
Data center customers include TCS and other data center builders; a nationwide multi-terabit DWDM network for a hyperscaler in India was won.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR1,500 crore order book include the BSNL 4G project, and how much will convert to revenue this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book excludes BSNL 4G; it is from India and international wireline and wireless customers, and a good portion is expected to convert to revenue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the NEC Massive MIMO deal in the order book, and how will it scale?
qa_highlights.answer: The first NEC PO is included in the INR1,514 crore order book; follow-on POs depend on the customer's rollout, and management expects them to be larger than the first.

qa_highlights.question: Is the BSNL 18,000-site add-on PO progressing and how fast can it be delivered?
qa_highlights.answer: Discussions are ongoing on sites and configurations; inventory is held, and delivery should be much faster as the sites are already commercial and tested.

qa_highlights.question: Are PAT-positive or breakeven targets realistic for FY27/FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not give financial guidance but that PAT-positive is the goal, with FY27 expected to show much better results and a path to profitability.

qa_highlights.question: How will receivables and inventory come down, and what if the BSNL add-on is delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: BSNL balance collections are expected significantly in FY27; receivables are shown net of BSNL advances in current liabilities. Inventory is usable across other global 4G/private network opportunities if BSNL is delayed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was intangible investment debt-funded, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not investing in technology evolution is a bigger risk in deep-tech; FY27 investment decisions will be more tightly tied to returns and business outlook.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company expecting order wins or growth targets over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical target given; management expects growth above FY24 levels excluding one-off projects and said the investments were sized for several times FY26 revenue.

risks_watch: BSNL 18,000-site add-on PO remains unsigned; timing uncertain, with inventory build-up at risk if delayed.
Receivables of INR3,258 crores and inventory of INR2,438 crores against FY26 revenue of INR1,103 crores; collection pace from BSNL is key.
Net debt of INR3,531 crores with gross borrowings of INR4,035 crores; cash of INR505 crores.
Memory and chip cost inflation and lead-time pressure on margins; extent of price pass-through not quantified.

Leadership transition: CFO Sumit Dhingra resigning effective May 15, 2026, with AVS Prasad appointed CFO from May 16; new COO and CEO appointments subject to shareholder approval; independent director change.
Intangible assets of about INR960 crores under development, with capitalisation dependent on commercialisation.
summary.management_tone: Confident about long-term positioning and AI-driven network demand, but cautious and sometimes evasive on near-term numbers: management declined revenue or deal-size guidance and called FY26 disappointing. Tone shifted to conciliatory on the call-timing and shareholder concerns.
key_quotes: So, with this trend, AI is going to drive a network infrastructure build super-cycle, which basically means that the current communication service provider networks, the CSP networks, will not be sufficient to handle the traffic growth in the coming years.
We needed a runway in FY26 to consolidate and transition our business beyond BSNL.
Yes, we've never given revenue or any other financial number guidance in the past.

But at the same time, we are positive about our future based on which we have made substantial investments during the year to make sure our products are ready, and technologically ready and capable for the business and the technology transition that we see.

growth.why: No numeric guidance; management calls PAT-positive FY27 a goal and expects a good portion of the INR1,514 crore order book (up from INR1,019 crore a year earlier) to convert in FY27, backed by the NEC 5G Massive MIMO and South Asia 4G orders, with no capacity additions disclosed.

mgmt.note: Senior management and CFO changes were announced during the call, but the brief gives no names, roles, or growth plans for the new leaders.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 FY26 EBIT loss narrowed to INR219 crores from INR239 crores and PAT goal is breakeven in FY27, but no numeric guidance and memory cost inflation is being passed through only partially.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or capacity additions disclosed; headcount ~2,300 broadly unchanged and inventory of INR2,438 crores already built ahead of the BSNL add-on.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book INR1,514 crores vs INR1,019 crores a year earlier (+49%), with management expecting a good portion to convert to revenue in FY27 from NEC 5G Massive MIMO and South Asia 4G orders.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex not discussed as a new program; intangibles under development rose to INR960 crores from INR400 crores, and FY27 investment decisions will be tied more tightly to returns, with no utilisation figure disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gives no numeric revenue or profit guidance, and FY26 revenue of INR1,103 crores with PAT loss of INR909 crores was called disappointing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: BSNL 18,000-site add-on PO is still unsigned and excluded from the INR1,514 crore order book, and receivables of INR3,258 crores against FY26 revenue of INR1,103 crores leave collection timing as a risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 5G 64TR Massive MIMO radio launched at India Mobile Congress, 1.2 Tbps to 1.6 Tbps optical scaling on the roadmap, and cloud-native 4G/5G core in multi-location trials.

rows.label: BSNL 18,000-site 4G add-on PO
rows.why: Sites are already commercial and tested with inventory held, so delivery would be fast if signed, but the PO remains unsigned and under discussion, and is excluded from the INR1,514 crore order book.

rows.label: BSNL collections drive receivables decline
rows.why: Management expects the remaining BSNL 4G collections to significantly happen in FY27, with receivables to decline progressively over the next few quarters from INR3,258 crores.

rows.label: Net debt of INR3,531 crores
rows.why: Gross borrowings are INR4,035 crores against cash of INR505 crores, and the FY26 PAT loss of INR909 crores gives no near-term path to lower debt from earnings.

tone.note: Management was confident on AI-driven network demand, NEC 5G Massive MIMO and FY27 order conversion, but declined numeric guidance and called FY26 disappointing; analysts pushed on the unsigned BSNL add-on, receivables and the PAT-positive timeline.
